newsitem.title: UK: New funds seek slice of European private equity.
newsitem.headline: New funds seek slice of European private equity.

text.p: The wave of corporate restructuring in continental Europe has driven a recent surge in interest from institutional investors looking to take advantage of private equity opportunities.

Three groups have launched funds in recent weeks, adding over 1.5 billion pounds ($2.4 billion) to the sector, amid the prospect of outperformance relative to quoted investment products. One of the largest groups of investors have been U.S. pension funds.

"(U.S. investors) are looking for new homes for their cash flows, private equity is seen to be very attractive and they are probably wanting to diversify their geographical spread as well. A lot of this money is coming from America," said 3i spokesman Charles Richardson.

Schroders Ventures, which last month launched a $1 billion private equity investment fund, said investors had been attracted by a track record since 1985 which generated compound annual returns of 25 percent versus a comparable 14 percent from European stock exchanges over ten years.
Its fund attracted subscribers from North America, Britain, continental Europe and Japan.
"The major corporate and industrial restructuring that is now taking place in continental Europe is expected to lead to a number of attractive investment opportunities," Schroders said.
Other recent launches include Charterhouse Development Capital's 800 million sterling buy-out fund -- the largest of its type -- which will invest in established businesses across Europe.

3i Group said on Thursday it was close to a preliminary closing of its second continental European co-investment fund, raising some 200 million sterling from institutional investors and committing a similar amount from its own funds.
Other funds active in the sector include CVC European Equity Partners, Electra Private Equity Partners and HSBC Private Equity Partnership Scheme.
"Increasingly the emphasis in the continental buyout market is shifting towards non-core disposals by the larger, more internationally-oriented companies", said Schroders partner Charles Sherwood.
3i's Richardson said private and public equity markets were opening up on the continent, bringing good opportunities. There was more appreciation of what equity capital can do.

"The UK is a very well developed venture capital market. In comparison the continental countries are very under-developed and I think its is inevitable that Schroders, Charterhouse and ourselves and lots more will increasingly pay attention to that."
